subject: Using stat_bin(origin= ) with a Date variable

messages.author: 8757f45da80a9e6c
messages.subject: Using stat_bin(origin= ) with a Date variable
parts:
Hi,

I have a data frame (df) with the variable obs.date (of type Date).
There thousands of observations (rows) spread over 9 months.
The observations are of a few different type, indicated by the categorical variable obs.type.
I want to show how the distribution of observations over types varies by time (to 1 week resolution).
The following code does what I want:

require(ggplot2)
require(scales)

# test - produces plot
ggplot(df, aes(x=enquiry_date)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(fill=bureau_score.type), binwidth= 7) +
  scale_x_date(breaks="1 month", minor_breaks="1 week")

The first date in the data is 2012-12-10 ().which is a Monday.
The histogram bars appear to run from Thursday to Wednesday.
I would like the histogram bars to count observations from Monday to Sunday to avoid the first bar being a partial week and to align the bars with the minor breaks grid lines.
I thought supplying an origin parameter to stat_bin would do what I wanted.

# test - gives error messages - no plot produced
ggplot(df, aes(x=enquiry_date)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(fill=bureau_score.type), binwidth= 7, origin=as.Date("2012-12-10")) +
  scale_x_date(breaks="1 month",
               minor_breaks="1 week")

This produced some error messages:

Error in seq.Date(origin, max(range) + binwidth, binwidth) :
  'to' must be a "Date" object
Error in as.environment(where) : 'where' is missing

I tried a couple of other ideas, like explicitly specifying the breaks to stat_bin but they all gave errors revolving around doing arithmetic with breaks.

What should I be doing here?

Thanks

Ross
